## findings

### F1 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED: mislabelled `method` leaves the repeat-test-fee computation with no method factor

- Symptom: `meter_ext_repeat_test_fee` declares one `method` factor, `repeat_fee_lookback`; its tiers are "earlier tests are counted over the demand-schedule look-back" (24 months), "... the residential look-back" (6), "... the meter type's free_test_period_months" (12).
- Root cause: the three tiers substitute a different number of months into one unchanged count ("The repeat escalation multiplier counts the earlier customer-requested tests of the same meter requested within the escalation look-back ..."); compute `tf_lookback_months` is a number fed into `tf_earlier_tests`. That is a `parameter` effect.
- Evidence: meter.extended.yaml `meter_ext_repeat_test_fee.factors[repeat_fee_lookback]` (effect: method; ladder 24/6/12 via `K('demand_schedule_window_months')`, `K('residential_window_months')`, `P('free_test_period_months')`); compute `tf_lookback_months`, `tf_earlier_tests`.
- Demonstrated consequence: relabelled honestly, the computation's factors are 5 parameters and 0 methods — below the floor of 1 `method` per computation. On this world the scored fee 960.00 is decided entirely by numbers swapped into one formula (500 x 2.0 + 60 - 100).
- Affected: charter `meter_ext_repeat_test_fee.factors`; task 1 `computations[policy_id=meter_ext_repeat_test_fee]`.
- Charter-global source: `_difficulty.md` factor_ladders F-LADDER-1.

### F2 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED: the refund months-reached ladder's taken tier is a treatment no utility would publish

- Symptom: `fast_refund_months_reached` and `settlement_refund_months_reached` tier 1 date the over-registration back to installation precisely because the customer's recent tests found the meter accurate.
- Root cause: rule text "the customer's complaints show the error may predate every test (a customer test that had found the meter outside tolerance would have taken it out of service, so each of those tests found it within tolerance), and the billing months the fast-meter refund reaches back are all the whole calendar months between the installation date and the company test date" (and the parallel sentence of the referee refund settlement). A recorded within-tolerance test is the utility's evidence that the meter registered correctly on that date; the base charter's own `error_start_basis` anchors the error at "the later of the installed date and the last previous test date".
- Evidence on this world: P's results `31b905eb` 100.21 (2024-11-18), `ef79fdd4` 100.12 (2025-03-17), `938f6644` 100.18 (2025-06-23), `732123fa` 100.27 (2025-10-20) and `e85453df` 100.42 (2026-08-10, customer-witnessed, field) are all within the type's +/-0.5 tolerance; the tier nonetheless refunds 18 counted-back bills (2025-03-20 .. 2026-08-20), every one of them inside the span those tests certified.
- Demonstrated consequence: the scored FR 8096.42 and RR 1905.16 rest on this tier; the standard method anchored at the latest accurate test gives FR 2484.61 and RR 0.00. The factor bears weight only through a tier whose method contradicts what the line of business treats as authoritative evidence.
- Affected: charter `meter_ext_fast_meter_refund` and `meter_ext_referee_refund_settlement` rule sentences and `factors[*_months_reached]` tier 1; task 1 `computations` for FR and RR.
- Charter-global source: `_difficulty.md` factor_ladders F-LADDER-2.

### Observations (not grounds for rework)

- Repeat fee E4 is a net-zero movement for the customer: the 960.00 fee is charged and returned by FR in the same call, and it cancels out of RR (skip TF -> RR still 1905.16). The edge bears weight on FR's own value as required.
- Persona: the reactive authorisation names the warehouse ("including anything at the warehouse"); not volunteered, does not name the backbill.
- Charter-global observations in `_difficulty.md` findings item 3 have no consequence on this world (bill windows coincide; interest tier 18/19 both >= 12; no post-test customer request; one owed fee only).
- Relation to previous revisions: first audit of this difficulty; no prior revision.
